description: We are Hornbill Void, a passionate Sarawak-based team leveraging coding, AI, and graphic design to build the ultimate Space Mission Design Game.
summary:
Kenyalang AR is software for astronauts, built by Team Hornbill Void under the Sarawak Space Initiative for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The name comes from Kenyalang, the Iban word for the rhinoceros hornbill, Sarawak’s state bird.

The problem: On long missions, astronauts face physical deconditioning, isolation and stress, and they are far from family. The platform is a calm virtual home for astronauts, made to look after both body and mind.

What it does: Users turn 360 degrees through a VR home to reach these widgets:

Crew Link: a working chat with crewmates and NASA Mission Control. Mission Control relays messages to the user’s family, with simulated Earth to space delay.
CtF Comms: latency-aware chat, plus Borneo photos with traditional music.
Health: vitals, eye screening and circadian care, and a Mental Wellness check-in with a breathing game and a personal statistics report.
Photos: an offline memory vault of photos from home.
Sleep Mode: a night scene that plays calming music and tracks heart rate until deep sleep.
Bio-Stimulation: guided sessions.

Safety and status: A clearance guide shows free space ahead (3.0 m) and turns yellow, orange or red as obstacles get closer. A status card shows ship link, battery and the crew member’s NFC card. The mascot Spacey guides users and answers questions about the team and the project.
details:
Kenyalang AR: Project Details

Overview

  • Name: Kenyalang AR. Kenyalang is the Iban name for the rhinoceros hornbill, Sarawak’s state bird.
  • Tagline: AR Software for Astronauts.
  • Team: Hornbill Void, under the Sarawak Space Initiative. Motto: Explore, Innovate, Inspire.
  • Event: NASA Space Apps Challenge.
  • Type: An interactive virtual home for astronauts, made as one web page (Main_dc.html) that runs in a browser or a headset.

Problem

Long deep-space missions strain the body and mind:

  • Physical deconditioning, including eye changes from spaceflight.
  • Isolation and sleep disruption.
  • Distance from family and Earth.
  • Little awareness of the physical space around the astronaut when wearing a headset.

Solution

A calm, easy-to-use VR environment that looks after both physical and mental health. The user turns 360 degrees to move between the widgets.

Features

Widget

What it does

Crew Link

Working chat with crewmates and NASA Mission Control, with quick replies and voice notes. Mission Control can relay a message to the astronaut’s family, with simulated Earth-to-space delay (12 min 30 s), and books a call slot.

CtF Comms

Latency-aware chat, plus Borneo photos with traditional music.

Health

Vitals, SANS eye screening, circadian care, and a Mental Wellness tab. Wellness has a mood check-in, advice for each mood, a breathing game and a statistics report (wellbeing score, stress, mindfulness, sleep, family chats).

Photos

Offline memory vault of photos from home. The Christmas Season photo plays “Somewhere In My Memory”.

Sleep Mode

Night scene with calming music and a heart-rate readout that settles. The screen goes black at deep sleep.

Bio-Stimulation

Guided sessions.

Safety and status

  • Clearance guide: An arc shows free space ahead, from 3.0 m. It is yellow at 2 m or more, orange between 1 and 2 m, and red at 1 m or less.
  • Status card: Ship link signal, battery with estimated time left (a full charge is 24 h, with alerts below 30% and 15%), and an NFC crew card for unlocking doors.
  • Environment: Full VR or Mixed Reality using the live camera. Mixed Reality needs https or localhost.

Spacey, the mascot

Spacey guides users, answers questions about the team and project, and gives the “Psst, crew!” hint on Crew Link. The page also has a “Meet Our Teams” page, a welcome page with the shining logo, and an ending page.

Team

  • Leonardi Wee You King
  • Ling Zhong Han
  • Caden Teo Kah Wei
  • Isaac Lim Yee Lun
  • Julius Chiew Zhen Hao

Technology

  • Single HTML page built on a React-based design component (support.js, vendor/react.js, vendor/react-dom.js).
  • Runs from a local server (start-server.bat or start-server.sh).
  • The soundtrack playlist is built from assets/ (default track: A Thousand Years, piano version).

Current limitations

  • Health values, heart rate, battery, signal and clearance are sample data. They can be replaced with real sensor input.
  • The “Meet Our Teams” photos and the other media in assets/ are placeholders until you add your own files.
  • The product is a VR experience with Mixed Reality support, so the “AR” in the name may need a short explanation.
